meta.disclaimer: Unofficial, student-made planning tool. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Stanford University, Stanford Law School, or the SLS Registrar. Course information was compiled from the SLS course catalog and class schedule grid as of Nov 10, 2026, is provided for convenience only, and may be incomplete, outdated, or incorrect. It is provided “as is,” without warranties of any kind, and is not academic advice or a guarantee of enrollment. Always confirm course details, meeting times, and deadlines in Axess, the SLS course catalog, and official Registrar communications before enrolling. The creator is not responsible for errors or omissions or for any decisions made in reliance on this site.

typeDefinitions.Doctrinal: Teaches a body of substantive law (cases, statutes, rules); usually a lecture graded mainly by an exam.
typeDefinitions.Seminar: Non-doctrinal: discussion, skills, theory or practice-oriented courses; usually graded on papers, assignments and participation.
typeDefinitions.note: SLS does not officially label courses as doctrinal or seminar; those labels are judgment calls based on each course's format, subject matter and grading.

notes: Constitutional Law, Criminal Law and Federal Litigation in a Global Context are required; you are auto-enrolled and your section is assigned in Axess.
1Ls may take up to 5 elective units, only from the 1L Winter Elective list, with no more than 14 units total.
In the Axess Law Lottery you can rank up to 4 lottery courses and be admitted to at most 2. 2Ls and 3Ls get preference over 1Ls.
Admitted and waitlisted students must attend every class during add/drop or tell the instructor in advance ("attend or inform").
